summary: myseliasan gains an immutable audit log of sensitive control-plane actions. A new append-only audit_log table (entities/audit_log.go) and IAuditService (services/audit.go) record who did what, to what, with what outcome, whenever an operator adopts/releases a node (node.adopt/node.release, the latter noting certificate revocation), rotates the fleet key (fleet.key_rotate — the key value itself is never recorded), changes a user's role/enabled state or elevates them to superadmin (rbac.set_role/rbac.set_disabled/rbac.elevate, with before->after role captured), grants or revokes per-node access (node_access.set/node_access.revoke), or sends a mutating command through the reverse node tunnel (node.command, covering the single choke point through which remote wipe/factory-reset/settings-writes reach a node; read-only GET/HEAD tunneled traffic is not audited). A node reporting its own unpairing (node.self_dropped) is attributed to the node rather than an operator. Recording is best-effort and never blocks or fails the action being audited. The trail is readable only via a new superadmin-gated GET /api/audit endpoint (apis/audit.go), with a matching Audit Log page in the SPA (filter by action/target, under Administration) added to the side-nav, App shell, and i18n (en/ms/zh/ar).
compatibility: Backward compatible for existing installs: a new audit_log table is created by bootstrap's additive schema reconciliation on next startup, no existing tables or columns change. audit_log is distinct from the existing api_log (HTTP access log with retention-based deletion) and is deliberately never purged — operators should account for its unbounded growth in their own retention/backup planning. No new config keys are required; the new /api/audit endpoint is superadmin-only and has no effect on any other role.
